Common questions

What does an AI trainer do?

You grade or write material used to train and test AI models: rating answers, comparing two responses, writing expert questions, or reviewing code. The work is remote and paid hourly or per task.

Do I need a degree?

Depends on the role. Generalist rating jobs mostly ask for strong written English. Law, medicine and STEM roles ask for a degree or license, which the platform checks during sign-up.

Where does the pay figure come from?

From the company’s own listing. We show it unchanged. Rates can move after a listing is posted, so confirm on the application page.

Does One AI Trainer take a cut?

No. Some links carry a referral code, and the platform pays us a small bonus if you are hired. Your rate is the same either way.

How long does it take to hear back?

Usually one to three weeks. Most platforms start with an assessment, then a short wait for a project to open. Some never reply if there is no match, so it is reasonable to apply to a few.

Can I apply from outside the US?

Often, yes. Mercor, Turing, Micro1 and AfterQuery hire in many countries. DataAnnotation is mostly US, UK, Canada and Australia. Meridial lists US and Canada roles plus some worldwide English work.

How often is this list updated?

Once a day. Listings that close are removed, and new ones appear the next morning. The date at the top of the page shows the last refresh.

Can I hold roles on more than one platform?

Yes. Most are independent contracts with no exclusivity, and many trainers work on two or three at once. Check each platform’s terms to be sure.

Independent listings aggregator. Not affiliated with Mercor, DataAnnotation, Turing, Meridial, Micro1 or AfterQuery. Pay is set by each company and may change. Some application links include a referral code. Created by Chaney Lovellette · LinkedIn
